_comment: Single source of truth for the confirmed Panorama P1 SysEx display protocol vocabulary. Loaded directly by src/lib.rs (see protocol_spec()) so this file, not a hand-duplicated match statement, is the actual data every binary in this crate reads from. The narrative evidence for every entry here (byte sequences, photos, test methodology) lives in research/panorama-p1-protocol-notes.md -- this file is the structured summary of that doc's 'Tenth finding' (page templates) and DISPLAY_ID enum, not a replacement for it.

page_templates.name: reset
page_templates.description: Genuine reset sentinel -- title bar still writes, but field writes have zero effect. Not a real page.

page_templates.name: message
page_templates.description: One-shot message overlay (writeMessageToDisplay's fixed shape, not the general compose shape). Unused by the real driver with actual content. Capped near ~127 total bytes.

page_templates.name: menu
page_templates.description: Generic browser/menu. displayId 4 sets the bottom menu-button row (confirmed with the real 'Browser/Preset/Remote/Pages' example).

page_templates.name: transport_launcher
page_templates.description: Transport Launcher (identity confirmed from source). Shows L:/R: loop-locator bars plus a 2x4 grid.

page_templates.name: list
page_templates.description: One fader plus a vertical bulleted list. Genuinely capped at 5 visible entries (confirmed by resending 16 and still only seeing 5) -- a real widget limit, not under-testing.

page_templates.name: grid5
page_templates.description: Plain 2x4 button grid, no fader/knob widgets at all. Matches source evidence for the Instrument macro/envelope sub-view.

page_templates.name: list_highlighted
page_templates.description: Discovered via a full numeric page_template sweep (Fifteenth finding), not from Bitwig's driver source. A list-like widget with one row shown highlighted/selected (blue bar) and small row-number labels (1, 2, ...) on the left. Not otherwise characterized.

page_templates.name: scene_buttons
page_templates.description: Discovered via the sweep (Fifteenth finding). Shows 4 buttons labeled S1-S4 plus a single-letter 'B' indicator to their left -- plausibly a scene/clip-launch quick-select row. Not otherwise characterized.

page_templates.name: browser_list
page_templates.description: Discovered via the sweep (Fifteenth finding). A vertical list of up to 8 numbered rows, each paired with a 'Pre' (Preset?) label on the right -- plausibly a browser/preset-list view. Templates 8 and 9 rendered indistinguishably in testing (9 may just be 8 caught after the list fully populated); not conclusively split apart yet.

page_templates.name: browser_list_alt
page_templates.description: See template 8 -- rendered identically to it in every test so far. Kept as a separate confirmed-valid id (isolated fresh test proved 9 is NOT a no-op, unlike 10+) pending a test that actually distinguishes it from 8.

page_templates.name: mixer
page_templates.description: 4x2 knob grid. The default page shown ~500ms after a real Bitwig session connects.

page_templates.name: mixer_alt
page_templates.description: Same 4x2 knob grid as template 16; not distinguished from it by any test so far.

page_templates.name: instrument_layer_container
page_templates.description: 8 faders split visually into two groups of 4. ctrlElementName (displayId 6) has 16 usable slots here (not 8) -- each fader shows two stacked labels.

page_templates.name: faders_row_a
page_templates.description: 8 faders in one continuous row (not split). Not distinguished from template 20.

page_templates.name: drum_pads
page_templates.description: 4x4 pad grid, rows A-D (bottom to top). Corrects an earlier under-tested claim of only 8 labelable pads: sending all 16 ctrlElementName entries (like template 18) labels all 16 pads individually, one label per pad (not stacked). displayId 0 (padState) does NOT label pads, confirmed no effect -- it's an on/off state field, not text.

page_templates.name: drum_pads_3row
page_templates.description: Confirmed genuinely DISTINCT from template 21 (Sixteenth finding), not the same family: a 3x4 pad grid, rows A-C only (12 pads). Sending all 16 ctrlElementName entries fills X1-X12 across the 3 rows; X13-X16 are not rendered anywhere -- there is no 4th row in this template at all, unlike 21's full 4x4. This is also the HIGHEST valid page_template value: an exhaustive 0-255 sweep (Seventeenth finding) confirmed every value from 23 through 255 is a no-op.

display_ids.name: pad_state
display_ids.description: Pad on/off/lit state. Confirmed NOT a text field -- sending 16 text entries had zero visible effect on template 21's pad labels. CONFIRMED FROM SOURCE (Twenty-third finding, OutputState.prototype.send()): only ever sent when pageTemplate is 21 or 22, as a single raw byte value per pad (not text) via a 9-value clip-state enum (off/on/recording/queued/etc) -- matches our hardware finding exactly, no further binary-payload testing needed.

display_ids.name: title_bar
display_ids.description: 3-segment title bar. Confirmed universal/identical behavior across every real template tested (2, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20, 21, 22). Confirmed 'global chrome': survives switching to a different real template untouched, unlike content fields.

display_ids.name: big_font
display_ids.description: currentParameterInfo. The large single-line readout seen as 'MIDI CC N' in every native screenshot. Real semantic role is touch/parameter feedback, not a permanent slot -- see protocol notes 'Twelfth finding'. Confirmed 'global chrome' (Fourteenth finding): survives a switch to a different real template untouched, same as title_bar.

display_ids.name: current_parameter_value
display_ids.description: currentParameterValue -- confirmed via a full numeric displayId sweep (Fifteenth finding), not from Bitwig's driver source. Renders in the top-right of the big-font row, paired with displayId 2 (name) directly to its left -- name+value for whatever's currently being touched. Behaves as chrome like displayId 2/1/4: survived every subsequent template switch tried.

display_ids.name: menu_button
display_ids.description: Bottom menu-button labels. Confirmed to work on template 16 as well as template 2 -- not template-specific. Confirmed 'global chrome' (Fourteenth finding): survives a switch to a different real template untouched, same as title_bar and big_font. CONFIRMED FROM SOURCE (Twenty-third finding): the per-button highlight/'on' state is NOT part of this SysEx field at all -- it's a plain Control Change, CC 106-110 (one per button), tested on hardware with the tab row actually populated and still showed no visible effect (negative result, now source-confirmed rather than guessed). The per-button 'type' (a 2-value enum) IS part of this SysEx field, sent as a special entry with index 0 (not a normal 1-based text index), length 5, followed by 5 raw type bytes -- sent before the 5 normal per-button text-label entries. Not yet replicated ourselves.

display_ids.name: page_labels
display_ids.description: Named in source (transport position labels). Confirmed a real, working text field (Nineteenth finding): a single entry renders as a small label near the first knob position, similar location to ctrl_element_name. Tested with only 1 of its 3 named slots filled; full slot-count/position mapping not characterized.

display_ids.name: ctrl_element_name
display_ids.description: Up to 8 slots for most templates; confirmed 16 slots specifically for template 18 (instrument_layer_container), rendered as two stacked labels per fader. Confirmed 'per-template content': cleared by switching to a different real template, even when the switching message never touches this field -- the only field confirmed to behave this way (Fourteenth finding), unlike title_bar/big_font/menu_button which are all chrome.

display_ids.name: ctrl_element_value
display_ids.description: Paired value field for ctrl_element_name (indices 1-8); confirmed to compose correctly alongside displayId 6 when sent in the same session. CONFIRMED FROM SOURCE (Twenty-third finding, OutputState.prototype.send()): genuinely shared with faderElementValue, at indices 9-16 (ctrlElementValue uses 1-8, faderElementValue uses 1+b+8 for b in 0..8) -- the index-arithmetic in the real driver, not just an inferred comment. Still assumed per-template like displayId 6 by analogy, not directly isolated for persistence.

display_ids.name: page_menu
display_ids.description: IDENTIFIED FROM SOURCE (Twenty-sixth finding) and CONFIRMED ON HARDWARE (Twenty-seventh finding): this is Bitwig's patch/preset/category BROWSE POPUP MENU (menuHandler.showMenu in the real driver), not an unused/reserved field as first thought (corrects the Twenty-third finding). Up to 8 visible items per page (indices 1-8), paginated in steps of 8 up to MAX_PAGEMENU_ITEMS=24 total; the up/down triangles seen on hardware (Nineteenth finding) are PAGE-scroll indicators, not per-item scroll. Built via a hand-constructed SysEx string (not the normal OutputState.send() path), always targeting page_template=0 (the reset sentinel) as an overlay regardless of whatever template is actually active -- CONFIRMED on hardware: populating it overlaid cleanly on top of an already-showing template 21 pad grid without disturbing it. The currently-highlighted item within a page is communicated separately via a plain Control Change (CC 111 = selectedMenuItem) -- CONFIRMED on hardware: CC 111 = 3 highlighted row 3 (red/pink bar), CC 111 = 5 moved the highlight to row 5. Dismissing it (clearMenu's bytes, 06 00 08 00 00) is CONFIRMED NOT to visually clear the popup by itself on this hardware -- likely needs pairing with a genuine page_template redraw of whatever was showing before, not yet isolated. Attributed to us only after a properly isolated blank-first-then-set-one methodology (an earlier attempt without blanking between steps falsely implicated ids 33/34, which were just stale leftover content -- see the Nineteenth finding writeup).

notes: Writes are partial updates within one template: unaddressed slots keep whatever they last held (stale content from an earlier write), never blanked automatically. See the per-display_id 'persists_across_template_switch' field for what ALSO survives switching to a genuinely different real template: title_bar, big_font, AND menu_button are all confirmed global chrome that survives a switch untouched (Fourteenth finding -- broader than first thought); ctrl_element_name (and presumably ctrl_element_value, its paired field) is per-template and gets cleared by a switch even when untouched by the switching message. pageTemplate=1 (the 'message' one-shot overlay) is a separate, special rendering pathway and not representative of switching between real content templates.

There is no read-back capability in this protocol: nothing can query the device's actual current screen content. Any client's notion of 'current state' is only ever a record of the last write it knows about.

page_template is NOT a free 0-255 byte in practice: only a specific allow-listed set of values (0-9, 16-22) is recognized -- CONFIRMED EXHAUSTIVELY across the full 0-255 byte range (Seventeenth finding), not just sampled. Sending an unrecognized value is a silent no-op -- the write has zero effect, and the display keeps showing whatever the last VALID template rendered (or the default post-connect mixer screen, if no valid template has been set yet this session). It does not error, glitch, or reset. See 'Fifteenth' and 'Seventeenth' findings in the protocol notes for the sweep methodology and the isolated-fresh-session tests that distinguish a real no-op from stale/cached content.

Sending the EXIT sequence (EXIT_1/EXIT_2, as every msg_test invocation does on its way out) resets the display back to its default post-connect appearance (default title bar, mixer/knobs widget, generic CC numbering) -- confirmed by a fresh capture taken well after a prior process's exit had already run. A screenshot taken after a test binary has fully exited is not evidence of what that test actually rendered; capture must happen during the live session, synced to the process's own output, not to an external wait/notification that may resolve after exit.

display_id addressing appears to be template-independent in terms of WHICH fields exist: every id tried (1, 2, 4, 6) is addressable regardless of which page_template is active, and the template only determines which widget renders the content fields. Whether a given field's CONTENT persists across a template switch is a separate question -- see 'persists_across_template_switch' above.
